subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A 68-year-old female is admitted with an exacerbation of Congestive Heart Failure (CHF). She has 3+ pitting edema. The dietician recommends a diet restriction to help manage her fluid retention. What is the standard sodium restriction often prescribed for this condition?
options: Sodium restriction is not necessary for CHF.
questions.explain: CHF patients retain fluid. Sodium restriction (typically 2000 mg/day or 2g/day) helps reduce fluid retention and edema. Higher intakes exacerbate symptoms.

questions.q: A client taking Warfarin (Coumadin) for atrial fibrillation asks if they should eat spinach. What is the appropriate advice?
options: Completely avoid spinach and all green leafy vegetables.
Eat as much spinach as desired; it has no interaction.
Maintain a consistent daily intake of Vitamin K-rich foods like spinach.
Stop taking the medication if eating spinach.
questions.explain: Warfarin works by antagonizing Vitamin K. Sudden changes in Vitamin K intake can alter the INR. Patients should not avoid Vitamin K but must keep their intake *consistent*.
